To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
turkeys can tolerate TI concentrations of 4.4 to 6.2 TI units/g of diet, but the AME of these diets is reduced.
turkeys can tolerate TI concentrations in SBM of 3 mg/g of diet, and that the AME of SBM is reduced when TI concentrations are 5 to 7 mg/g of SBM.
turkeys tolerate soybean trypsin inhibitor concentrations up to 3 mg/g of diet.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of soybean trypsin inhibitor (TI) and urease on turkey performance and the utilization of diets containing these soybean products.
the effect of soybean meal (SBM) trypsin inhibitor (TI) on turkey performance.
the use of undertoasted SBM in turkey diets.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the tolerance level of turkeys to trypsin inhibitor in soybean meal is dependent on the age of the bird and the level of dietary protein.
turkeys tolerate 3 to 4 mg TI/g of SBM in diets containing 40 to 50% of SBM.
the TI content of SBM can be tolerated by turkeys through 3 wk old at levels up to 2.5 TI/g of diet; however, turkeys 6-8 wk of age could tolerate 3 TI/g of diet.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
turkeys can tolerate TI concentrations of 3 mg of TI/g of diet when fed diets containing 40 to 50% soybean meals with urease indices of.2 or less.
soybean meal with a TI of 3 mg/g can be used in turkey diets through 3 wk and 4 mg/g through 8 wk.
turkeys are more tolerant of trypsin inhibitor in soybean meal than are chickens.
The main takeaway from our work is that
turkeys can tolerate a wide range of soybean TI activity, and that it does not appear to be a problem in practical diets.
the TI of soybean meal can be used in diets for turkeys up to 3 weeks of age without adverse effect.
soybean meals high in urease activity can be fed to turkeys without adverse effects.
